title: gateway: ingress payload windowing + bounded fncall streaming to reduce memory/latency spikes
author: Asha Menon
commits: 6 commits: 9c3a2f8 add ingress windowing primitives and docs; a52b7d1 enforce per-route max_payload_bytes and default window; bf4e6c0 bound fncall stream buffers and add backpressure signals; d1f0b9a update openai-compat adapter to honor chunk-policy; 3a1f4b6 add integration tests for large fncall streams; f7c8b2e squash: finalize route-config defaults and metrics
description:
Context: We observed intermittent memory spikes and increased tail latency when many concurrent function/tool calls arrived as large initial payloads (tool params + long messages) on the gateway ingress. These events were correlated with long-lived streaming connections where the proxy would buffer large chunks while waiting for downstream runtime availability.

Motivation: Reduce gateway memory amplification and improve tail latency without breaking existing OpenAI-compatible streaming semantics. We need to limit per-connection and per-route buffered bytes, apply a small sliding "window" for ingress chunk acceptance, and surface clear backpressure behavior to callers and runtimes for graceful degradation.

Design summary: 1) ingress window: implement a sliding byte window per connection that caps buffered, unconsumed bytes to route-configurable max_payload_bytes and a new streaming_window_bytes (defaults: max_payload_bytes=1MB, streaming_window_bytes=128KB for OpenAI-compat routes). The window allows a few small chunks to stream through while preventing a single large upload from inflating memory. 2) fncall streaming bounds: when function/tool calling is detected (via content flags in the OpenAI-compat adapter), the gateway keeps a tighter default window and switches to chunk-prioritization: small chunks (<4KB) are preferred and put through immediately; large chunks are acknowledged with a 429-like backoff signal (X-Stream-Accept: delayed) and reflowed when capacity frees. 3) route-level overrides: new fields in route_defaults.yaml and per-route config to tune both limits and prioritization behavior. 4) observable signals: new metrics (gateway.ingress.windowed_bytes, gateway.ingress.backpressure_count) and a short human-readable reason code in responses when chunks are deferred. 5) compatibility: openai_adapter updated to interpret and emit the new small-chunk prioritization header and to surface a stable fncall handshake when chunks are deferred so SDKs can retry with smaller chunks.

Checklist: - [x] ingress window primitives and tests - [x] route config + defaults - [x] fncall prioritization logic - [x] adapter compatibility changes + unit tests - [x] integration test that simulates many concurrent fncall streams with mixed chunk sizes - [x] docs and release notes

Testing: Added gateway/tests/streaming_integ_test.go that spins up a simulated runtime and opens 300 concurrent streams mixing small/large payloads. Verified memory usage under the new defaults is stable and tail P99 latency drops ~35% in our stress harness. CI initially failed the integration flakily due to a timing assumption; fixed by adding backpressure delay jitter handling and reran checks.

Rollout plan: feature flag gated under "gateway.ingress.windowing.v2". Default enabled on staging, will flip in prod after 48h of staging telemetry. If early signals show increased client errors we will lower streaming_window_bytes for OpenAI-compat routes and push a hotfix to relax prioritization.

Backward compatibility: No breaking API changes. OpenAI-compatible streaming still follows same framing; we add advisory headers and observable reason codes. SDKs are recommended but not required to honor the backpressure headers. Documented behavior in docs/gateway/payload-policies.md.
review_comments: Diego: Can we make the 4KB small-chunk threshold configurable at route-level? I think mobile clients may prefer 8KB. (resolved: added route override)
Lina: The metric names look fine but add a tag for route.id so we can filter noisy tenants. (resolved)
Samir: Integration test flaked on 2nd CI run, I saw a flakiness because of tight timing; ask authors to add jitter. (resolved)
Asha: responded with implementation notes and added jitter + route tag in metrics
release_notes: Gateway: add ingress streaming window and fncall prioritization to reduce memory amplification and improve tail latency for streaming function/tool calls. Defaults tuned for OpenAI-compatible routes; route overrides available.
